summary: GROUND-phase adversary: scans a contract plus the grounded code for forced, lasting, costly-to-reverse choices that are NOT in the contract Decisions section and that the human would care about — so no key decision is silently defaulted and bites later.
logs: hunted 2 candidate undecided choices across 5 lenses; filtering to what the human would care about

autoResolved.choice: Whether the new AG0040/AG0041 tests model real InternalsVisibleTo between their compiled fake reference assembly and the fake subject assembly, and whether the shared analyzer-test runner surfaces compiler diagnostics so a fixture that fails to compile cannot produce a green positive test.
autoResolved.resolution: Both are required, and neither is optional. AG0041's fake Engine source declares the members the rule is about as `internal` and carries `[assembly: InternalsVisibleTo("guard")]` and `[assembly: InternalsVisibleTo("AgentGuard.TestHelpers")]`, so the Acceptance 8 accept case is genuinely accessible and its assertion turns on the analyzer rather than on CS0122. AnalyzerRunner asserts the compilation produced no compiler errors before returning analyzer diagnostics, so no positive test can pass on a fixture the compiler already rejected. The route is the non-disruptive one — a no-compiler-error assertion inside AnalyzerRunner, not swapping GetAnalyzerDiagnosticsAsync for GetAllDiagnosticsAsync, which would change what every existing Assert.Single/Assert.Empty across the 48 analyzer test files means and would collide with the contract's 'Do not reverse any test assertion other than the two named in Acceptance 7'. Which of those two routes is taken is implementation, not a decision.
autoResolved.principle: best-practices-guide area 6 (Proof), 6a — 'Prove behavior with a test, and watch it fail before it passes, so the test actually exercises the behavior' and 'Never scaffold or wire a check to pass, and never hard-code an expected value just to match what the code currently does.' Reinforced by rails-test-code rail 6 'Every assertion can fail' (Violation: an assertion 'that passes regardless of the code') and rail 2 'RED before green'.
autoResolved.evidence: /Users/timothystockstill/code/macos/4thWAIV/agent-guard/analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/AnalyzerRunner.cs:132 returns only GetAnalyzerDiagnosticsAsync(), and RunWithReferenceAsync (lines 57-76) builds the reference compilation with no InternalsVisibleTo mechanism. /Users/timothystockstill/code/macos/4thWAIV/agent-guard/analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/BoundariesToCrossPlatformOneDoorAnalyzerTests.cs:15-28 shows every existing cross-assembly fake declared `public static class`, so no existing test depends on internal accessibility. Contract Acceptance 8 (.dev/inprocess/74-pre-work-move-system-services/contract.md:158) requires AG0041 to ACCEPT an invocation of the internal SystemServices.Create() from `guard` and `AgentGuard.TestHelpers` compilations — an Assert.Empty that would pass identically if the compiler had already rejected the reference, which is precisely rails-test-code rail 6's 'passes regardless of the code'. Neither the contract's Surfaces list (contract.md:94-110) nor its Reuse ledger (contract.md:112-129) touches AnalyzerRunner.cs, so nothing else settles it. Contract MUST NOT (contract.md:147) 'Do not reverse any test assertion other than the two named in Acceptance 7' forces the non-disruptive route.

autoResolved.choice: How 'lexically inside AgentGuard.Engine.SystemServices.Create()' is defined for the shared method-level caller check used by AG0040 and the new Engine gates on AG0023/AG0029 — specifically whether a permitted door or factory call written inside a lambda or a local function nested in Create()'s body is permitted or reported.
autoResolved.resolution: Take the narrowest reading that works: the call site's own containing method symbol must BE the static `Create` method on `AgentGuard.Engine.SystemServices`, matched on assembly, namespace, type name, method name, and staticness together through the existing WellKnownType.IsInAssembly conjunction. A call nested inside a lambda or a local function within Create() is NOT permitted and is reported; permitting it later requires an explicit rule change, on exactly the footing the contract already gives a fifth factory ('A fifth factory in Boundaries is rejected until this rule is changed to name it'). The check is written explicitly and pinned by a test that asserts the nested-lambda call is reported, rather than left to whatever SyntaxNodeAnalysisContext.ContainingSymbol happens to return per construct. This costs nothing today and fails loudly rather than silently widening the hole.
autoResolved.principle: best-practices-guide area 3 (Security & trust honesty), 3a 'do these without asking' — 'Take the least privilege and the narrowest scope that works.' The permission carve-out in a guard rule is a privilege scope, so the narrowest workable definition is the required one. (5a was deliberately NOT cited: .dev/inprocess/74-pre-work-move-system-services/adjudication.md:5 records Tim overruling a 5a-based stretch on this same contract.)
autoResolved.evidence: The narrowest reading works for every case the contract requires to be accepted: /Users/timothystockstill/code/macos/4thWAIV/agent-guard/src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/SystemServices.cs:86-107 shows Create()'s body is entirely top-level statements — CrossPlatformAdapters.Create() at :90, PlatformServices.Create() at :91, and the four adapter factories at :93-96 — with no lambda and no local function, and contract.md:137 forbids changing that shape ('leave its shape, service instances, and construction order exactly as they are'). Acceptance 2, 5, and 7 (contract.md:152, :155, :157) only require the door call written directly in Create()'s top-level body. The approved decisions bound the permission tightly — contract.md:24 'and only from AgentGuard.Engine.SystemServices.Create()', contract.md:25 'No access is granted to another method in SystemServices or to another Engine class', contract.md:26 'A shared analyzer helper may implement these checks, and must not broaden the permitted calls', and MUST NOT at contract.md:147 'do not permit any caller other than AgentGuard.Engine.SystemServices.Create()'. The rule-change-on-widening precedent is contract.md:57. Reversal cost is one predicate plus its test in /Users/timothystockstill/code/macos/4thWAIV/agent-guard/analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/CompositionPoint.cs (EnclosedBy at :94-107 is the file the contract's reuse ledger at contract.md:120 already names as the owner), so the choice is cheaply reversible and local — the agent's under the rails-decisions boundary once the principle fixes its direction.
